title: customer-zeta-incident-timeline-draft-maya-khan
content:
Summary:
Quick working notes / timeline for Customer Zeta outage on 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-24. This is a scratchpad to capture commands, error snippets, hypotheses and the internal comms draft to send to CS/AM and customer. Not a final PM.

High level symptom:
- Customer Zeta reported increased 5xx rates and timeouts for text-generation routes using model redmx-large-v1 in region eu-west-1 starting ~2026-02-22 13:12 UTC. Errors observed: 504 Gateway Timeout, grpc UNAVAILABLE, and occasional OOMs on worker nodes.

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-22 12:58 UTC: Customer reported first slow responses via Zendesk ticket #487. They said latency > 5s for short prompts.
- 2026-02-22 13:12 UTC: Monitoring alerts triggered (per-route error rate > 3%). Pager notified eng-sre on-call (Ethan P.).
- 2026-02-22 13:18 UTC: On-call started triage. Verified increased error rates on /v1/generate/redmx-large-v1 route. KPI dashboard: token throughput unchanged, but active connections spiked by ~2.3x for that customer.
- 2026-02-22 13:25 UTC: Ran quick health checks on serving fleet. Noted elevated CPU on gateway proxies and increased KV cache misses for redmx-large-v1.
- 2026-02-22 13:41 UTC: Attempted mitigation: increased per-route concurrency cap from 12 -> 18 for customer Zeta (temporary). Partial reduction in 504s but some nodes reported transient OOMs.
- 2026-02-22 14:05 UTC: Rolled back concurrency change after OOMs; reverted to 12. Began capturing heap dumps and dmesg from affected nodes.
- 2026-02-22 15:10 UTC: Identified a spike of long-context requests (seq_len > 4096) hitting the model; correlated with a new batch job from customer that started at ~12:45 UTC. Confirmed that the job is using streaming with immediate token flush disabled (bulk requests).
- 2026-02-22 16:00 UTC: Customer advised to throttle the batch job; they applied temporary rate-limiting (throttled by 60%). Error rate decreased but latency still elevated during peaks.
- 2026-02-23: Continued collection of logs; observed repeated GRPC retries from client (UNAVAILABLE) and some gateway proxy 502/504 spikes coinciding with autoscaler spin-ups.
- 2026-02-24 09:30 UTC: Implemented KV cache warm-up for model variant (prepopulate prefixes from recent requests) in staging; tested improvement locally.
- 2026-02-24 12:10 UTC: Recommended to customer a config change: enable streaming-token-flush and reduce batch window for that job. Customer implemented change at ~12:45 UTC.
- 2026-02-24 13:00 UTC: Error rates returned to baseline; ticket moved to monitoring.

Commands run / snippets (captured outputs truncated):
- top on gateway-proxy-03:
  PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
  2431 root      20   0  1250m  423m  112m S  45.3 12.1   1:12.33 nginx

- kubectl logs -n inference pod/redmx-serve-7f5b2 -c runtime --since=1h | tail -n 200\  
  [2026-02-22T13:26:02Z] WARN runtime::kv_cache: miss for key prefix: user-zt-12345...
  [2026-02-22T13:26:10Z] ERROR runtime::memory: allocation failed: requested 2147483648 bytes, available 1530427392
  [2026-02-22T13:26:10Z] INFO runtime::shutdown: starting graceful shutdown

- dmesg | tail -n 20 (on worker that OOMed)\  
  [ 123456.789012] Out of memory: Kill process 1987 (redmx-runtime) total-vm:5400000kB, anon-rss:420000kB, file-rss:8000kB

- curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate... -d '{"model":"redmx-large-v1","input":"<redacted>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -w "\n%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
  => 504 8.24

Hypotheses (working):
1) Customer batch job sent many long-context streaming requests without immediate token flush -> runtime held large KV cache + attention state -> memory pressure -> OOMs and degraded latency.
2) Autoscaler reaction (scale up) + cold kernels for new instances caused transient latency spikes and grpc UNAVAILABLE responses while proxies retried.
3) Some gateway proxy configuration (keepalive / upstream timeouts) may be too aggressive for long streaming sessions, surfacing 502/504 to client instead of keeping streaming path open.

Evidence supporting hypothesis 1:
- allocation failed log shows requested ~2GB and available ~1.5GB around the same time OOM occurred.
- request payloads during spike have seq_len > 4096 (from request sampling).
- when customer reduced batch concurrency by 60%, error rates dropped significantly.

Evidence against hypothesis 1:
- not every OOM correlates with a long-context request; some OOMs were on nodes handling normal-length requests. Need to check whether other tenants' traffic caused additional pressure.

Immediate next steps (internal):
- Collect full request samples for redmx-large-v1 from 2026-02-22 12:30 -> 16:30 UTC (Lina has partial export). Action: Ethan to run export job (JIRA-ZETA-487-EXP).
- Gather heap snapshots + /proc/meminfo from affected pods; upload to S3 and share link.
- SRE to review autoscaler logs for scale-up latencies and kernel warm-up times.
- Validate gateway proxy timeout settings for streaming routes (current upstream_read_timeout=15s). Consider increasing to 60s for streaming routes.
- Create a transient mitigation: enforce per-client max-seq-len and max-concurrency at the gateway for known customers until we release more robust memory accounting.

Customer-facing comms (draft):
Subject: Follow-up on 2026-02-22 service disruption\nHi <Customer Zeta team>,\n\nThanks again for working with us to stabilize the workload. We traced the primary issue to a combination of long-context batch requests from your job and memory pressure on some serving instances. While we are continuing to investigate and harden the platform, the steps we took that improved stability were:\n- Temporary throttling of the batch job (reducing concurrency by ~60%)\n- Adjusted gateway routing to reduce retries during autoscaling\n- Implemented a temporary KV cache warm-up which reduced cold-start latency for new instances\n\nNext steps from our side:\n- Collect and analyze full request traces and heap dumps (ETA 48 hours)\n- Recommend keeping streaming token flush enabled and reducing batch window for large-context jobs\n- Follow-up with a permanent fix (better memory accounting + per-tenant limits) and timeline in the next update\n\nWe will share a more detailed technical postmortem once the investigation completes. Apologies for the disruption — we appreciate your patience.\n\nInternal note: keep this message soft and focused on remediation; escalate any billing/credits asks to CS leadership.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Do we have per-tenant memory isolation metrics? (quick answer: partial, need more sampling)
- Are other customers hitting similar long-context patterns around the same time? (Cross-tenant correlation ongoing)
- Should we push a gateway config change in prod immediately (increase upstream_read_timeout)? Risk: could mask real hangs; need SRE approval.

Logging / artifacts we should attach to final PM:
- request-samples-redmx-2026-02-22-12_30-16_30.json (Lina export)
- heap-dumps/ (S3 links)
- autoscaler-logs-2026-02-22-13:00-17:00.log
- nginx-proxy-stats-02-22-13.log

Notes to self (Maya):
- Follow up with Lina on export job status (she said it would finish by 02/25).
- Ask Observability team for a short script to compute per-tenant peak RSS over time (existing perf agent might do it).
- Draft final timeline after we confirm heap dump analysis (tentative PM draft due by 2026-03-06).

Slack snippets (for internal timeline):
- @ethan: \"seeing 5xx spike for Zeta, looking into redmx-large fleet\"
- @lina: \"export job started, will upload samples to s3://redwood-incidents/zeta/\"
- @maya: \"suggest temp gate: max-seq-len=4096 for customer-zt-12345 until PM done\"

If this doc becomes the PM, move to shared_drives/product/incident-reports and change status->in_review.

End of scratchpad.
